title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 102
paragraphs: When Demaratus heard this, he spoke as follows: “O king, since you bid me by all means to speak the truth, and so to speak as one who shall not afterwards be convicted by you of having lied, I say this: with Greece, poverty is always a native growth, but valor is one that has been brought in, gained by intelligence and the force of law. By means of this valor Greece defends herself continually, both against poverty and against a master's rule. Now, I have words of praise for all the Greeks settled in the Dorian lands, but what I am about to say concerns not all of them, only the Lacedaemonians. Of them I say, first, that there is no possibility they will ever accept your terms, which bring slavery to Greece; and second, that they will stand against you in battle even if all the other Greeks are on your side. As for numbers, do not ask how many they must be to do this. If a thousand of them have taken the field, they will fight with you — or if it is fewer than that, or more.”
